architecture.title: Four engines, one OpenAI API — run one at a time on a Spark
architecture.caption: The bake-off lab, LiteLLM and agents use one OpenAI client for every engine; only the base URL changes. vLLM and NIM share :8000, TensorRT-LLM uses :8355 (:8123 in the Nemotron Super recipe), SGLang :30000. Each engine reserves most of the 128 GB unified memory at start-up, so start one, measure it, stop it, then start the next.

sequence.title: Lab 06-3 — SGLang's prefix cache across two turns
sequence.caption: Turn 2 repeats turn 1's system prompt and question, then adds the answer and a new question. SGLang's RadixAttention finds the shared prefix in its cache and prefills only the new tokens; with --enable-cache-report the response says how many tokens came from the cache.

steps.label: no match → prefill all tokens, store the prefix

longest shared prefix found → reuse its KV

charts.title: Memory each engine reserves at its playbook default (128 GB Spark)
charts.caption: Arithmetic from the playbook defaults: fraction × 128 GB (not a measurement; TensorRT-LLM's fraction applies to memory that is free after the weights load). Any two of these together exceed one Spark, which is why the bake-off runs one engine at a time.

charts.title: Lab 06-2 scorecard — total across the seven needs
charts.caption: Sum of lab 06-2's scores (2 = validated path shown in the playbook, 1 = possible but not shown, 0 = no path). It measures documentation, not speed: use lab 06-1 on your Spark for speed.
